You are working in the Ligra graph-processing framework at /workspace.
The framework (/workspace/ligra/*.h) is COMPLETE and already implements
vertexSubset, edgeMap/edgeMapData/edgeMapDense/edgeMapDenseForward/edgeMapSparse/
edgeMapSparse_no_filter, edgeMapFilter, packEdges, vertexMap, vertexFilter,
vertexFilter2 and parallel_main. DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILE under /workspace/ligra/,
and DO NOT MODIFY /workspace/apps/Makefile or any other app's .C file.
Your ONLY writable file is the single .C file named in your task.

Build & run (apps/ has symlinks to ../ligra/*.h already):
  cd /workspace/apps && make <AppName>
Compiler line: g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <App> <App>.C

CRITICAL framework facts (verify by reading the headers before coding):
* In the default build, parallel.h maps parallel_for -> plain `for` (single
  threaded). Code must still be written with correct atomics (CAS/writeMin/
  writeAdd) as upstream Ligra does, but execution is deterministic.
* Types: uintE/intE (32-bit by default), uintT/intT, UINT_E_MAX, INT_E_MAX.
* ligra/utils.h provides: CAS, writeMin, writeAdd, hashInt, newA, granular_for,
  sequence::plusReduce, sequence::plusScan, pbbs::* . There is NO writeOr --
  if you need atomic bitwise-or, define it locally in your .C file.
* edgeMap signature:
    edgeMap(graph<vertex>& GA, VS& vs, F f, intT threshold = -1, const flags& fl = 0)
  flags available: no_output, pack_edges, sparse_no_filter, dense_forward,
  dense_parallel, remove_duplicates, no_dense, edge_parallel.
  threshold -1 means "use GA.m/20".
* The user struct F passed to edgeMap must provide update(s,d),
  updateAtomic(s,d) and cond(d). For WEIGHTED apps the signatures are
  update(s,d,weight) / updateAtomic(s,d,weight).
* vertexMap(VS& V, F f) calls f(v) for a plain vertexSubset.
* vertexFilter(vertexSubset V, F filter) -> dense-based result.
  vertexFilter2(...) -> sparse-based result.
* vertexSubset constructors: vertexSubset(n) empty; vertexSubset(n, v) single
  vertex; vertexSubset(n, m, uintE* sparseArray); vertexSubset(n, m, bool* dense).
  Methods: isEmpty(), numNonzeros(), numRows(), toSparse(), toDense(), del(),
  vtx(i), isIn(v), dense().
* cond_true(d) is provided for "always true" cond functions.
* Every app is a template function:
    template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>& GA, commandLine P) {...}
  It MUST be a template over vertex, because parallel_main instantiates it for
  symmetricVertex, asymmetricVertex, compressedSymmetricVertex and
  compressedAsymmetricVertex. Therefore ONLY use the vertex methods that also
  exist on compressed vertices: getOutDegree(), getInDegree(),
  decodeOutNgh / decodeInNghBreakEarly / decodeOutNghSparse /
  decodeOutNghSparseSeq / countOutNgh / packOutNgh / copyOutNgh.
  *** DO NOT call getOutNeighbor(j) / getOutNeighbors() / getInNeighbor(j) in an
  app *** -- those do not exist on compressed vertices and the app must keep
  compiling once Ligra+ compressed vertices are implemented. If you need the
  neighbour list, materialize it with copyOutNgh (see apps/Triangle.C for the
  exact idiom) or use countOutNgh with a predicate.
* Read /workspace/apps/BFS.C, /workspace/apps/PageRank.C and
  /workspace/apps/Triangle.C first -- match their style, comment density and
  the 23-line MIT licence header they carry.
* /workspace/tutorial/*.C contains SKELETONS with "//FILL IN" markers showing
  the intended structure of some apps. Use them as structural hints only.

Inputs: ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (symmetric, unweighted, n=128 m=708,
run with -s) and ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 (symmetric, WEIGHTED, run with -s).

Always finish by actually building and running your app and confirming the
output is sane. Report exactly what you ran and what it printed.


You are an INDEPENDENT VERIFIER for /workspace/apps/Components.C, which another agent just wrote.

The spec it was given was:
Implement /workspace/apps/Components.C -- connected components by label
propagation (the classic Ligra algorithm).
* uintE* IDs and uintE* prevIDs, IDs[i] initialized to i.
* CC_F: update(s,d) writes min(IDs[d],IDs[s]) into IDs[d] and returns 1 only
  when the original IDs[d] equalled prevIDs[d] (so each d is output once per
  round); updateAtomic(s,d) = (writeMin(&IDs[d],IDs[s]) && origID==prevIDs[d]);
  cond(d) = cond_true(d).
* CC_Vertex_F syncs prevIDs[i]=IDs[i], applied with vertexMap at the start of
  every round.
* Initial frontier = ALL n vertices (dense bool array).
* Loop until the frontier is empty.
* Report "Components rounds: <N>" and the number of distinct component labels
  as "Components: <N>" (count i where IDs[i]==i is NOT correct for label
  propagation with writeMin -- instead count the number of distinct values in
  IDs; do it simply and correctly, e.g. mark a bool array of size n).
* Run: ./Components -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100

Its report was:
**File written:** `/workspace/apps/Components.C` (only file created/modified; `ligra/`, `apps/Makefile`, and other apps untouched — the `M Makefile`/`M ../ligra/ligra.h` in git status predate this task)

**Commands run**
```
cd /workspace/apps && make Components
   -> g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o Components Components.C     (clean, no warnings)
cd /workspace/apps && ./Components -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
```

**Full stdout**
```
Components rounds: 4
Components: 4
Components rounds: 4
Components: 4
Running time : 1.5e-05
```
(Two result blocks are expected: `parallel_main` calls `Compute` once as a warmup, then `-rounds 1` timed run. `-rounds 3` gives three identical timed blocks, so `Compute` is idempotent / leaves no cross-round state.)

**Implementation**
- `CC_F { uintE* IDs, *prevIDs; }` — `update(s,d)` writes `min(IDs[d],IDs[s])` and returns 1 only when `origID == prevIDs[d]`; `updateAtomic(s,d)` is `(writeMin(&IDs[d],IDs[s]) && origID == prevIDs[d])`; `cond(d) = cond_true(d)`.
- `CC_Vertex_F` sets `prevIDs[i]=IDs[i]`, applied via `vertexMap` at the top of each round.
- Initial frontier: dense `bool[n]` all-1 → `vertexSubset(n,n,frontier)`; plain `edgeMap(GA,Frontier,CC_F(...))` (default threshold, no flags — the `prevIDs` snapshot already guarantees one output per `d`, so `remove_duplicates` from the tutorial skeleton is unnecessary).
- Distinct-label count: `bool seen[n]`, `seen[IDs[i]]=1`, then count set entries — not `IDs[i]==i`.
- Uses no `vertex` methods at all, so it stays compilable for compressed vertices.

**Correctness verification (independent)**
- Python union-find over `../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100` (n=128, m=708): **4 components**, sizes `[125,1,1,1]`, per-component minimum ids `{0,1,5,40}`.
- A throwaway instrumented copy (built in `/tmp`, since deleted) printed the surviving label set: `labels: 0 1 5 40` — exactly the union-find minima. Also consistent with `./BFS -s` reporting `BFS visited: 125` from vertex 0.

**Concerns:** none blocking. Two notes: (1) `Components rounds: 4` is lower than `BFS levels: 6` because in the single-threaded build `parallel_for` is a plain loop, so labels propagate several hops within one round — round count is schedule-dependent by design, while the component count/labels are not. (2) The distinct-label count is an intentionally simple O(n) sequential mark-and-count outside the timed kernel; it adds ~n work per `Compute` call, negligible here but worth knowing if this app is ever used for large-scale timing.

Your job: try to REFUTE that this app is correct and complete.
1. Read the file. Check it really implements the named algorithm (not a stub or a
   trivially-wrong shortcut), that it is `template <class vertex>`, and that it
   does NOT call getOutNeighbor/getOutNeighbors/getInNeighbor/getInNeighbors
   (those break on compressed vertices later).
2. Rebuild from scratch: cd /workspace/apps && rm -f Components && make Components
   -- it must compile with no errors. Warnings are acceptable.
3. Run it and check the printed numbers are actually right. Where feasible,
   compute the ground truth INDEPENDENTLY with a small python script over
   /workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (or rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 for the weighted
   app) and compare. Do not trust the implementation's own claims.
4. Confirm it does not modify anything under /workspace/ligra/, the Makefile,
   or another app (check: cd /workspace && git status --short).

If you find a real defect, FIX IT in Components.C (that file only), rebuild,
rerun, and re-verify. Then report.

Return: VERDICT (PASS or FIXED or BROKEN), the ground-truth values you computed
independently, the values the app printed, and anything still wrong.

import random, sys
def write(path,n,edges):
    # edges: list of (u,v) directed; symmetrize for -s style symmetric file
    adj=[set() for _ in range(n)]
    for u,v in edges:
        adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u)
    offs=[]; flat=[]
    for v in range(n):
        offs.append(len(flat)); flat.extend(sorted(adj[v]))
    with open(path,'w') as f:
        f.write("AdjacencyGraph\n%d\n%d\n"%(n,len(flat)))
        f.write("\n".join(map(str,offs))+"\n")
        f.write("\n".join(map(str,flat))+"\n")
    # ground truth components
    par=list(range(n))
    def find(x):
        while par[x]!=x: par[x]=par[par[x]]; x=par[x]
        return x
    for v in range(n):
        for u in adj[v]:
            a,b=find(v),find(u)
            if a!=b: par[max(a,b)]=min(a,b)
    comp={}
    for v in range(n): comp.setdefault(find(v),[]).append(v)
    lab=[0]*n
    for c in comp.values():
        mn=min(c)
        for v in c: lab[v]=mn
    print("%s n=%d m=%d comps=%d"%(path,n,len(flat),len(comp)))
    open(path+".labels",'w').write(' '.join(map(str,lab)))
    return lab

# 1. reverse chain: 0 - (n-1) - (n-2) - ... - 1  (forces ~n rounds of propagation)
n=200
order=[0]+list(range(n-1,0,-1))
write('/tmp/g_revchain',n,[(order[i],order[i+1]) for i in range(n-1)])

# 2. all isolated vertices -> n components
write('/tmp/g_isolated',50,[])

# 3. two cliques, interleaved ids (evens / odds) -> 2 components, labels 0 and 1
n=40
e=[]
ev=[i for i in range(n) if i%2==0]; od=[i for i in range(n) if i%2==1]
for grp in (ev,od):
    for i in range(len(grp)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(grp)): e.append((grp[i],grp[j]))
write('/tmp/g_twocliques',n,e)

# 4. random sparse graph, many components
random.seed(7)
n=500
e=[(random.randrange(n),random.randrange(n)) for _ in range(300)]
e=[(u,v) for u,v in e if u!=v]
write('/tmp/g_random',n,e)

# 5. single self-loop-free star centered at high id
n=64
write('/tmp/g_star',n,[(n-1,i) for i in range(n-1)])
EOF

import subprocess,sys
def run(g,labfile):
    out=subprocess.run(['/tmp/CCdbg','-s','-rounds','1',g],capture_output=True,text=True)
    lines=[l for l in out.stdout.split('\n')]
    labs=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('LABELS:')]

    rnds=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('Components rounds:')]

        g, out.returncode, [r.split(': ')[1] for r in rnds], [c.split(': ')[1] for c in comps],
        len(set(exp)), ok))
    if out.returncode!=0: print("  stderr:",out.stderr.strip()[:300])

VERDICT: **PASS** — no defect found, `Components.C` unchanged by me.

## What I ran

```
cd /workspace/apps && rm -f Components && make Components
  -> g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o Components Components.C     (exit 0, no warnings)
cd /workspace/apps && ./Components -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
cd /workspace/apps && ./Components -s -rounds 3 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
```

App output on `../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100`:
```
Components rounds: 4
Components: 4
Components rounds: 4
Components: 4
Running time : 1.6e-05
```
`-rounds 3` gives three further identical blocks -> `Compute` is idempotent, no cross-round state.

## Independent ground truth (python union-find, my own parser of the AdjacencyGraph file, symmetrizing as `-s` does)

| quantity | ground truth | app printed |
|---|---|---|
| n / m | 128 / 708 | (matches header) |
| number of components | **4** | **4** |
| component sizes | [125, 1, 1, 1] | — |
| surviving labels (per-component minima) | **{0, 1, 5, 40}** | **{0,1,5,40}** (verified, see below) |

I did not trust the printed count alone. I built a throwaway instrumented copy in `/tmp` (`sed` insert of a `LABELS:` dump, compiled with `-I/workspace/apps`; workspace untouched, since deleted) and compared **all 128 per-vertex labels** against the union-find expectation — exact match. I then repeated the full per-vertex label comparison on 5 adversarial graphs I generated with their own ground truth:

| graph | expected comps | printed comps | rounds | all n labels match min-of-component |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rMatGraph_J_5_100 | 4 | 4 | 4 | yes |
| reverse chain, n=200 (`0-199-198-…-1`, forces sparse frontier + `updateAtomic`, ~n rounds) | 1 | 1 | 200 | yes |
| 50 isolated vertices (m=0, so `threshold = m/20 = 0`) | 50 | 50 | 1 | yes |
| two interleaved cliques (evens/odds), n=40 | 2 | 2 | 2 | yes |
| random sparse, n=500, 592 edges, 205 comps | 205 | 205 | 23 | yes |
| star centered at highest id, n=64 | 1 | 1 | 3 | yes |

Extra hardening (all on copies in `/tmp`, never in the workspace):
* **Real parallelism:** rebuilt with `-DOPENMP -fopenmp` and re-ran the whole label comparison at `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1,2,4,8`. Every per-vertex label still matched ground truth; only the round count wobbled (e.g. random graph 21-23, revchain 199-200), which is expected schedule dependence, not an error.
* **ASan/UBSan/LSan build:** no out-of-bounds (incl. `seen[IDs[i]]`), no UB, and **no leak attributable to `Compute`** — `IDs`, `prevIDs`, `seen` and the initial `frontier` bool array are all freed exactly once (`del()` is NULL-safe, no double free). The only reports are pre-existing framework issues present for any app: an `operator new` / `free` alloc-dealloc mismatch between `IO.h:313` and `graph.h:116`, and a leak of `stringToWords`/`readStringFromFile` buffers in `IO.h`. Both are in `/workspace/ligra/`, outside this app's control.

## Spec conformance checks

* `template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>&, commandLine)` — yes, line 69-70 of `/workspace/apps/Components.C`.
* `grep` for `getOutNeighbor|getOutNeighbors|getInNeighbor|getInNeighbors` -> **no hits**. It uses *no* vertex methods at all, and the `-Wall` compile shows successful instantiation for `symmetricVertex`, `asymmetricVertex`, `compressedSymmetricVertex` and `compressedAsymmetricVertex`.
* `CC_F::update/updateAtomic/cond`, `CC_Vertex_F`, all-n dense initial frontier `vertexSubset(n,n,frontier)`, `vertexMap` at top of each round, loop to empty frontier, distinct-label count via `bool seen[n]` (not `IDs[i]==i`) — all present and byte-for-byte the upstream Ligra `CC_F` logic.
* Licence header is **identical to the first 23 lines of `BFS.C`** (`diff` clean).
* `prevIDs` is never read uninitialized: round 1's frontier is all n vertices, so `vertexMap` fills every entry before the first `edgeMap`. The invariant "`prevIDs[d] == IDs[d]` at the start of every round for *all* d" holds by induction (only changed vertices are output, and they are exactly the ones re-snapshotted next round), so the stale-`prevIDs`-for-non-frontier-d concern is a non-issue.

## Nothing else touched

`cd /workspace && git status --short`: only `?? apps/Components.C` and `?? apps/Components` relate to this task. `M apps/Makefile` (mtime 00:11:59) and `M ligra/ligra.h` (mtime 00:10:09) both predate `apps/Components.C` (mtime 00:45:11) and predate this task; the Makefile diff is only the pre-existing `ALL=` target list. Other `apps/*.C` and `ligra/*.h` entries belong to sibling agents' work, not this file.

## Still-open notes (non-defects)

1. `Components rounds: 4` < `BFS levels: 6` because the default build maps `parallel_for` to a plain `for`, so a dense pull round propagates labels many hops in index order. Round count is schedule-dependent by design (confirmed: it changes with thread count); the component count and the labels are not.
2. The distinct-label count is an O(n) sequential mark-and-count executed inside `Compute` but it is placed after the kernel; it is inside the timed region, so at very large n it would add a small constant to `Running time` (negligible here: 1.6e-05 s total for n=128). Upstream Ligra prints nothing, so this is a spec-mandated addition, not a bug.
